title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA INTERACTS WITH MERITORIOUS STUDENTS FROM EKLAVYA MODEL RESIDENTIAL SCHOOLS
subtitle: AIM HIGH AND STRIVE TO REALIZE YOUR DREAMS WITH DEDICATION, DISCIPLINE, AND SELF-CONFIDENCE: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU TO STUDENTS
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 NOV 2026 2:56PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu interacted with a group of meritorious students from Eklavya Model Residential Schools at Rashtrapati Bhavan today (November 12, 2026). This interaction was organised by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs as part of Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada, observed every year to commemorate the birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda.
Addressing the students, the President said that the nation is moving forward to achieve the goal of Viksit Bharat by the year 2047. The development of every region of the country and every section of society is essential. The Eklavya Model Residential Schools are not only providing quality education to tribal students but also offering them opportunities to hone their multifaceted talents. She stated that there is no dearth of talent in our country. What the students require are the right opportunities, a conducive environment, and proper guidance. She was happy to note that the ratio of boys and girls in Eklavya Model Residential Schools is equal. She said that it is a testament to country’s progress toward inclusive development.
The President urged students to aim high and strive to realize their dreams with dedication, discipline, and self-confidence. She said that education should not only be a means to earn a livelihood for themselves; rather, their goal should also be to create employment opportunities through their knowledge. She underlined that when our youth become job creators, the country’s inclusive development will gain further momentum.
The President advised students to be well-informed about current affairs and the changes taking place in the country and the world. This will help them develop logical thinking and analytical skills. She advised students that whenever they visit their village, they should share with their family members, relatives, and neighbours, the knowledge of current affairs and information about public welfare schemes being implemented by the government. Such efforts on their part will benefit their family and society, and will also add greater meaning and purpose to their education.

During the visit, Prime Minister will participate in the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit (EAS), being hosted by the Philippines as the ASEAN Chair for 2026 on 17 November 2026.
​India-ASEAN relations are a central pillar of India's Act East Policy and our vision for the Indo-Pacific. The visit comes as India and ASEAN are celebrating 2026 as the ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation, and will commemorate 35 years of Dialogue Relations and five years of our Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in 2027.
The ASEAN-India Summit will review progress in the implementation of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, including the ASEAN-India Plan of Action 2026–2030, and chart the future direction of cooperation.
The East Asia Summit will provide an opportunity to exchange views on matters of regional and global importance with ASEAN and other participating countries.

title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi participates in the Kisan Tak Bharat Agriculture Conference 2026
subtitle:
Agricultural development, smarter farming and farmer empowerment are key to building a Viksit Bharat: PM

The solar power revolution of the PM-KUSUM scheme has transformed the country's Annadatas into Urjadatas : PM

We move forward with the concept of 'Lab to Land': PM

Namo Drone Didis are demonstrating how advanced technology can be effectively used in village: PM

India offers growing opportunities in everything from agri-engineering to agri-startups. The focus is on empowering farmers to become agricultural entrepreneurs: PM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 NOV 2026 10:47PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today participated in the Kisan Tak Bharat Agriculture Conference 2026. Addressing the gathering on the occasion in the presence of agricultural scientists, agri-entrepreneurs, and farmers from across the nation, the Prime Minister commended the media group for its enthusiastic past participation in the cleanliness campaign and for dedicating two full days to organizing this innovative Kisan Mela.
Noting that the conference is taking place amid a festive atmosphere just days after Deepavali and during the ongoing Chhath Mahaparv, which is deeply rooted in agrarian life, the Prime Minister pointed out that major Indian festivals such as Bihu, Pongal, Onam, Baisakhi, Sarhul, and Pola are intrinsically tied to farming. “Meaning, agriculture and farming are our culture, our tradition, and the foundation of our social life,” observed PM Modi.
Recalling his Red Fort address on the seven streams of national strength (Saptadhara) required for a Viksit Bharat, in which agriculture serves as a primary pillar, the Prime Minister emphasized that the significance of such farmer conferences has grown manifold because national development depends directly on agricultural modernization. “The building of a Viksit Bharat is simply not possible without developing agriculture, without making farming smarter, and without empowering the farmer,” asserted Shri Modi.
Illustrating the close link between agricultural growth and national progress through a widely discussed World Bank study showing that 50 crore Indians escaped poverty in just 12 to 13 years with a sharp decline in rural poverty among small farmers and farm laborers, the Prime Minister highlighted that this period coincided with India's agriculture sector achieving an average growth rate above 4 percent for the first decade since independence.
Observing that farmers and agricultural experts understand the necessity of continuous policy and methodological evolution, the Prime Minister  pointed out that as global markets, dietary habits, weather patterns, and technologies evolved over time, farmers needed to be empowered afresh. “Merely filling the granaries of food grains is not enough,” asserted Shri Modi.
Highlighting the steps taken over the past decade to match the pace of global agricultural change and boost farm incomes through annual agricultural exports exceeding 4 lakh crore rupees, the Prime Minister noted that India now ranks first globally in the production of milk, pulses, jute, rice, and millets, and second globally in wheat, cotton, fruits, vegetables, and fish production. “These are not merely a few figures, they show how much the capability of India's farmers has increased,” observed PM Modi.
Emphasizing that farmer prosperity requires moving beyond traditional reliance on wheat, rice, and sugarcane, the Prime Minister stated that the government is actively promoting crop diversification and allied agricultural activities.
Tracing India's agricultural trajectory from achieving food grain self-reliance through the Green Revolution and becoming the world's top milk producer through the White Revolution, the Prime Minister detailed the past decade's rapid expansion across multiple sectors, including a nearly 70 percent rise in milk output, a nearly 90 percent surge in egg production, a more than twofold increase in fish production under the Blue Revolution, a jump in honey output from around 80,000 tonnes to 1.5 lakh tonnes under the Sweet Revolution, and horticulture production rising from 280 million tonnes to over 350 million tonnes. “Today I have given you figures which show that this journey is now moving forward in a very grand manner,” noted PM Modi.
Explaining that integrating these diverse agricultural revolutions under a comprehensive vision generates multiple income streams essential for future farming, the Prime Minister spotlighted the solar power revolution under the PM KUSUM Yojana, which has provided nearly 12 lakh solar pumps to reduce electricity bills and enable farmers to earn revenue by generating solar power in their fields. “This revolution has turned the Annadata of the country into an Urjadata, and along with production in farming, we have also focused on productivity and the farmer's profit,” asserted Shri Modi.
Recalling his recent completion of 25 years as head of a government and his continuous efforts as Chief Minister of Gujarat to modernize agriculture through grand Krishi Mahotsavs, the Prime Minister described how hundreds of agricultural scientists and experts traveled across villages in 40 to 45 degree heat to inspect farm soil, assess water availability, and advise cultivators on suitable crops and practices. “We moved forward with the concept of Lab to Land, ensuring that the knowledge present in the labs of scientists reached the farmer's field directly, and the farmers of Gujarat got a massive benefit from this,” remarked PM Modi.
Stating that his governance experience in Gujarat proved invaluable at the national level, the Prime Minister noted that the number of soil testing labs across India has grown from a few hundred in 2014 to over 8,400 today alongside more than 725 Krishi Vigyan Kendras, while livestock health has been prioritized through a massive vaccination drive against Foot and Mouth Disease. “To protect livestock from Foot and Mouth Disease, free vaccines have been administered to the livestock of more than 8 crore farmers,” noted Shri Modi.
Challenging the outdated mindset that rural India cannot adopt advanced technology, the Prime Minister pointed out that Namo Drone Didis have proven skeptics wrong by skillfully operating drones to spray fertilizers and pesticides. “Now the scope of its use is also being expanded,” observed PM Modi.
Highlighting the expanding role of engineering in Indian agriculture as scientists, engineers, and youth collaborate to develop cost-reducing sowing and harvesting machinery alongside affordable, sensor-based and AI-equipped tools that provide precise data to even the smallest cultivators, the Prime Minister emphasized the push toward farm-level value addition and converting Annadatas into agri-preneurs across a thriving ecosystem of agri-engineering and agri-startups. “In recent years, small farmers together with the government have built a massive network of 10,000 FPOs, which is making groups of small farmers into value creators and connecting them with food processing and export markets,” noted Shri Modi.
Stressing that the government's clear policy and intent is to ensure farming does not burden cultivators, the Prime Minister pointed out that India has spent 16 lakh crore rupees over the past 12 years to provide affordable fertilizers despite international price spikes caused by the ongoing war in Iran and the Gulf region. “A bag of DAP fertilizer which costs 5,000 rupees is being made available to the farmers of India for 1,300 rupees, and a bag of urea which costs 3,000 rupees in the international market is being given for less than 300 rupees,” observed PM Modi.
Sharing an exclusive revelation on how the government shielded farmers when the escalating West Asia war drove crude oil prices from 70 dollars to 122 dollars per barrel within weeks and created pressure to hike diesel prices by at least 50 rupees per liter while neighboring countries raised fuel rates by 40 to 50 percent, the Prime Minister stated that the government refused to pass the international market shock onto citizens and farmers, raising diesel by just 7 rupees per liter while absorbing 43 rupees per liter itself at a monthly cost of 14,000 crore rupees to date. “When the interest of the country's farmers is paramount and when there is the spirit of Nagrik Devo Bhava, then such sensitive decisions are taken,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Concluding his address by acknowledging the monumental achievements of Indian farmers in recent years and calling for even greater efforts to build a Viksit Bharat with prosperous farmers, thriving villages, and modern, profitable agriculture, the Prime Minister expressed confidence that the deliberations at the conclave would benefit the nation before extending his best wishes. “The better suggestions and solutions that have emerged from here, the government will also work on them,” affirmed Shri Modi.

title: English rendering of PM's address at the Kisan Tak Bharat Agriculture Conference
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 NOV 2026 10:09PM by PIB Delhi
content:
You also have my heartfelt greetings on this sacred festival of Diwali, and with the programme of Chhathi Maiya also approaching, I extend my very best wishes for that as well. My greetings to all of you.
Chairman and Editor-in-Chief of the India Today Group, Shri Arun Puri ji, the agricultural scientists, agri-entrepreneurs, farmer friends, and all distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen who have come from across the country for this programme.
First of all, I wholeheartedly congratulate the India Today Group for this innovative initiative. When the country launched the cleanliness campaign, the India Today Group participated in it very enthusiastically. Now you have organised this Kisan Mela, and dedicated two full days to it. This is a very positive beginning. I congratulate all of you. And Arun ji speaks such excellent Hindi, so double congratulations for that.
Friends,
This event is taking place at a time when the country is in a festive mood. Two or three days ago, we celebrated the festival of Diwali, and now the spirit of the Chhath Mahaparva is all around us. The festival of Chhath is deeply connected with agricultural life, and in our country, most festivals are linked with farming and agriculture. Bihu, Pongal, Onam, Baisakhi, Sarhul, Pola, many such festivals are connected with agriculture. In other words, farming is our culture, our tradition, and the foundation of our social life.
Friends,
From the Red Fort, I had spoken about the seven streams of strength for a Viksit India, and among these, agriculture is a principal stream. Building a Viksit India is simply not possible without developing agriculture, without making farming smarter, and without empowering farmers. That is why the importance of such farmer conferences becomes even greater.
Friends,
You can understand the relationship between farming and the country's progress through two important facts. Recently, a World Bank study on poverty was released, and it is being discussed across the world. It states that within just 12–13 years, 50 crore poor people in India have defeated poverty. It also states that poverty has declined very rapidly in villages. This means that a large number of small farmers and agricultural labourers have overcome poverty. Now look at the coincidence. During the past decade, India's agricultural growth rate has remained above 4 percent. This is the first decade after Independence in which the country's agriculture sector has achieved an average growth rate of more than 4 percent, for the first time since Independence. And during this same period, a large number of poor people in villages have defeated poverty. But unfortunately, people trapped in angles and agendas of news coverage fail to notice this achievement of the country.
Friends,
Those engaged in farming and experts connected with agriculture know how necessary continuous change in agricultural policies and methods is. Those who governed for decades became satisfied merely because the country's farmers had filled the grain warehouses of the nation. But what did farmers receive after that? Merely filling grain warehouses is not enough. Over time, the world changed, markets changed, people's needs changed, eating habits changed, the weather changed, and technology changed. Along with these changes, we needed to empower our farmers in a new way. But earlier, even this was not given attention.
Friends,
Over the past decade, the country took steps to match this pace, and the results are before all of us. Today, India exports agricultural products worth more than four lakh crore rupees every year, and this money is increasing the income of our farmers. Today, India is number one in the world in milk production. Today, India is number one in pulse production. India is number one in jute production. India has also become number one in rice production. It is number two in the world in wheat production. It is number two in the production of cotton, fruits, and vegetables. It is number two in fish production, and India is also the world's largest producer of millets. These are not just statistics. They show how much the capability of India's farmers has grown.
Friends,
One more thing is necessary for the prosperity of India's farmers. It is necessary that they do not remain dependent only on traditional crops such as wheat, rice, and sugarcane. I repeat, farmer brothers should not remain dependent only on wheat, rice, and sugarcane. Therefore, the government is also placing emphasis on other crops and other activities related to agriculture. Let me remind the India Today Group of something. The word “revolution”, kranti, is something the India Today Group is particularly fond of. Therefore, I am now going to talk about a few revolutions.
Friends,
There was a time when the country took a historic step towards self-reliance in food grain production through the Green Revolution. After that, the White Revolution made India the world's largest milk producer. Today, I will give you some more figures that show how this journey is now moving forward with remarkable momentum. Over the past decade, India's milk production has increased by nearly 70 percent, 70 percent. Egg production has also increased by nearly 90 percent, 90 percent. And if we talk about the Blue Revolution, India's fish production has more than doubled in a decade. New opportunities have emerged in the field of beekeeping through the Sweet Revolution. Honey production has increased from around 80 thousand tonnes to 150 thousand tonnes. In horticulture as well, India's production has increased from 280 million tonnes to more than 350 million tonnes.
Friends,
When we connect all these revolutions with a broader vision, multiple sources of income are created for the country's farmers, and this is very essential for the future of agriculture. Let me give you another example. Another revolution, the solar power revolution. This revolution has transformed the food provider into an energy provider. Under the PM-KUSUM Scheme, nearly 12 lakh solar pumps have already been distributed. This is reducing farmers' electricity bills, and farmers have also begun earning income by installing solar plants on their fields. Along with production, we have also focused on productivity and on farmers' profits.
Friends,
Recently, I completed 25 years as the head of government. When I was the Chief Minister of Gujarat, I was continuously working to modernise agriculture even then. At that time, I started large agricultural festivals. I remember that in May and June, in temperatures of 40–45 degrees Celsius, hundreds of agricultural scientists, agricultural experts, and progressive farmers would come together. We would prepare Kisan Raths and travel in them. We would go to villages and to fields. We would visit farmers' fields and interact directly with them. What type of soil the area had, what the availability of water was, which crops could perform well there, what kind of farming was required, every such issue would be discussed directly with farmers. Our effort was that the knowledge present in scientists' laboratories should directly reach farmers' fields. In other words, we moved forward with the concept of Lab to Land, and Gujarat's farmers benefited greatly from it.
Friends,
The experience from my Gujarat days has been extremely useful after coming to the central government. In 2014, there were only a few hundred soil-testing laboratories in the country. Today, their number has increased to more than 8,400. Just as pathology laboratories are expanding in medical science, today soil-testing laboratories are expanding. Today, there are more than 750 Krishi Vigyan Kendras across the country. We are also prioritising the protection of animals from diseases. To protect livestock from Foot and Mouth Disease, more than eight crore farmers' animals have received free vaccinations. During COVID, we provided free vaccines, and everyone remembers that. But this is Modi; he provides free vaccines even to animals.
Friends,
Often, some people with old ways of thinking believe that the use of large-scale technology will not be possible in our villages. The Namo Drone Didis have proved such people wrong. Once, while speaking with all the Drone Didis through video conferencing, I was talking to a daughter from a village, perhaps in Jharkhand. She told me, “Now my status has changed.” I asked, “Why?” She said, “The entire village calls me a pilot, and even my younger brothers-in-law call me ‘Pilot Bhabhi’.” Just imagine how much self-respect increases. At present, the Namo Drone Didis are using drones for spraying fertilisers and pesticides. Now the scope of their use is also being expanded.
Friends,
Today’s India is also expanding the role of engineering in agriculture. Our agricultural scientists, engineers, and youth are together developing such tools and machines that are reducing the cost of farming. In some places, machines are being developed that are making sowing and harvesting easier. And I would especially like to urge the people from industry present here, those engaged in manufacturing equipment for farmers, as well as our startup founders, that whatever equipment you build from now on should be powered by solar energy, because we are taking solar power to every farm. Just as the whole world has now rushed towards electric vehicles, I am in favour of making every type of agricultural tool solar-powered. And I am also making considerable efforts in that direction. But I would urge all MSMEs and small-scale industries to focus on this. This is going to become a very large area of revolution. Not only that, sensor-based equipment equipped with AI technology is now being developed that can provide precise information to farmers and can be affordable even for the smallest farmers. Arrangements are now being developed for soil testing through mobile phones. You simply place a little soil on the mobile-based device, and your phone immediately provides a report identifying which crop your soil is suitable for, how much fertilizer is required, and what type of fertilizer is needed. In other words, just see how rapidly change is taking place. Today, from agricultural engineering to agri-startups, India is full of opportunities. We must transform our food providers into agri-preneurs, that is, agricultural entrepreneurs. Work is now progressing rapidly across the country on how value addition can take place right where production happens.
Friends,
In the past few years, small farmers, working together with the government, have built a large network of 10,000 FPOs, that is, Farmer Producer Organizations. These are turning groups of small farmers into value creators and connecting them with the food-processing business. I clearly remember one incident from my days in Gujarat. In Gujarat, we introduced the Jyotigram Yojana. We separated agricultural feeders from domestic feeders and began supplying as much electricity to farmers as possible. This greatly benefited farmers. There are some villages near Gandhinagar where most people cultivate chillies. But farmers there faced a problem. If production increased, prices would fall, and if production declined, earnings would decline. They suffered in both situations. If too many chillies were produced, they could not sell them. But after the arrival of electricity through the Jyotigram Yojana, they started converting chillies into red chilli powder. They packaged that powder, got advertisements made, printed photographs of personalities on the packaging, and began selling chilli powder on a large scale. Through this value addition, they became highly successful earners. Earlier, they could not even obtain a proper price for their chillies, but now their products became brands. This shows what becomes possible when attention is given to every small aspect. Efforts to connect small farmers with export markets are also progressing rapidly.
Friends,
Our policy and our intent are absolutely clear. It is our priority that farming should not become a burden on farmers. To ensure affordable fertilizers for farmers, the country has spent ₹16 lakh crore over the last 12 years. Friends, this is an enormous figure. Sixteen lakh crore rupees is more than the annual budget of many countries. Amid the war currently taking place around Iran and the Gulf countries, a bag of DAP fertilizer that costs ₹5,000 is being made available to Indian farmers for only ₹1,300. A bag of urea that costs ₹3,000 in the international market is being provided to Indian farmers for less than ₹300.
Friends,
I would like to mention one more subject, and I have spoken about this before as well. For your network, what I am about to say today is exclusive.
Friends,
When the war situation in West Asia was escalating, the price of crude oil rose from 70 dollars to 122 dollars per barrel within just a few weeks. At that time, India also faced a major challenge. India was in a situation where diesel prices should have been increased by at least ₹50 per litre. An increase of ₹50 per litre had become necessary. At that time, the government took a decision in the interest of farmers. We decided that the full burden of the shock in international markets would not be passed on to citizens and farmers. The government increased diesel prices by only ₹7 per litre, whereas the required increase was ₹50. The government itself absorbed a burden of ₹43 per litre. In neighbouring countries as well, diesel prices had increased by 40 to 50 percent. But that did not happen in India. Since then and up to today, the government has been bearing a loss of ₹14,000 crore every month. Every month. Yet we did not allow harm to come to the country's farmers. When the welfare of farmers is the highest priority, when there is a spirit of Citizen Devo Bhava, such sensitive decisions are taken.
Friends,
Amid so many discussions about the national interest, I am sure the people of Aaj Tak must be wondering that no negative headline has emerged so far. So perhaps now we should discuss something that can become a headline. Until now, I have been talking about the country, and perhaps that has not attracted as much media attention. So now let me talk about controversy.
Friends,
Nowadays, some people pull the Constitution out of their pockets. The country understands very well what they are doing. They seem to think that the nation's Constitution and democracy are sitting in their pocket. Even while not being in power, they remain intoxicated with the mindset of power. But when these very people were in power, what were their actions like? Let me narrate a small incident.
Friends,
You may remember that there was a time when people in the media used to rank the best-performing states. In one such ranking related to the economy, Gujarat was ranked number one, and at that time I was the Chief Minister of Gujarat. The institution that gave Gujarat the number one ranking was named after a former Prime Minister of India. That hint is enough; you can find the name yourselves. This ranking was based on research conducted by some of the country's most respected economists. But the people sitting in power in Delhi did not like Gujarat receiving that recognition. They formally instructed those conducting the research that things could not continue this way. They said that from then onward, no report could be published without their approval first.
Friends,
That was the situation then, and today those very people go around delivering lectures on tolerance and democracy. And when exactly did this happen? What happened after that? You can research and find those details yourselves. Let me now move towards concluding my remarks.
Friends,
Without doubt, the achievements of the country’s farmers over the past years have been remarkable. To build a Viksit India, we now have to expand our efforts even further. We must create a future where farmers are prosperous, villages are prosperous, and agriculture is modern and profitable. I am confident that the deliberations taking place here will benefit the country. The government will also work upon the best suggestions and solutions that emerge from here. And since I have come among you today, I would certainly like to make one appeal. At the beginning, Anjana ji said in her introductory remarks that farmers are connected to two things: the food provider and Mother Earth. I want to ask my farmer brothers and sisters: are we really protecting this Mother Earth of ours? Ask yourselves honestly. The way we are destroying Mother Earth through excessive use of chemicals, and we are her children. We are killing this mother before our own eyes. If we do not wake up in time, if we do not make efforts to save Mother Earth, then the mother who nourishes us today may one day leave our hands. Such a situation could arise. That is why the government has emphasized natural farming. Those who have experimented with natural farming have achieved great success. A single cow can provide sufficient manure for natural farming on 30 acres of land. No chemical inputs are required. Many such subjects must have emerged during your discussions today. Therefore, I appeal to all farmers that we should move towards chemical-free farming. I am not talking about organic farming; I am talking about natural farming, and every farmer can adopt it easily. We can take steps to save our soil by becoming free from chemicals. One challenge with our farmer brothers and sisters is that until they see something with their own eyes, they do not accept it. No matter how many long speeches are delivered, farmers do not simply accept something. They believe only after seeing it. Otherwise, all that stays in their minds is that they must apply the yellow powder, use the green bottle, use the green container, bring the red container, and if the neighbour uses two bags, they will use two bags too; if the neighbour uses four sacks, they will use four sacks too. This is the responsibility of all of us, and especially of progressive farmers, to free them from this mindset. We must help them move towards chemical-free natural farming. The first task is to save our Mother Earth. This mother is capable of providing everything we need. She will never let us feel any shortage, provided we protect her. We are the children of Mother Earth. It is our duty to fulfil this responsibility as her sons and daughters, as the children of Mother Earth. With this confidence, I extend my best wishes to all of you. I also congratulate the India Today Group. You have undertaken a task that will greatly help the nation in the years ahead.
Thank you very much.

title: CCRAS-CARI and University of Delhi sign MoU to document medicinal plant diversity of DU North Campus
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 NOV 2026 5:25PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS) - Central Ayurveda Research Institute (CARI), New Delhi and the University of Delhi signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on 10 November 2026 to undertake a collaborative project titled “Inventory of Phyto-diversity of Medicinal Importance Used in Ayurveda of North Campus of Delhi University.”
The MoU was formally signed by Prof. (Vd.) Rabinarayan Acharya, Director General, CCRAS, and Dr. Vikas Gupta, Registrar, University of Delhi, at the VC Office, North Campus, New Delhi.
The project aims to systematically document, identify and conserve the medicinal plant diversity available across the 250-300 acres of the University of Delhi's North Campus. The initiative seeks to explore the rich botanical heritage of the campus and document plant species of medicinal importance described in Ayurveda.

The project will also result in the preparation of an illustrated pictorial book documenting the medicinal flora of the North Campus, along with joint research publications to disseminate the scientific findings.

This collaborative initiative represents an important step towards strengthening institutional cooperation in the fields of Ayurveda, biodiversity conservation, medicinal plant research and scientific documentation. title: Naturopathy Day 2026: Scientific Research Strengthens India's Nature-Based Healthcare Ecosystem
subtitle: 9th National Naturopathy Day to be observed on 18 November at Nagamangala, Karnataka, under the theme ‘Prakrutik Chikitsa, Swasth Bharat’
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 NOV 2026 12:12PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Naturopathy in India is gradually moving beyond its traditional association with nature cure towards a more structured ecosystem of scientific research, clinical evaluation and preventive healthcare. With growing attention to lifestyle-related disorders, obesity, stress and healthy ageing, its emphasis on nutrition, natural therapies and lifestyle modification is finding renewed relevance.
The 9th National Naturopathy Day will be observed on 18 November 2026 at the Central Research Institute of Yoga and Naturopathy (CRIYN), Nagamangala, Karnataka, under the theme
“Prakrutik Chikitsa, Swasth Bharat.”
The day is observed to promote awareness of naturopathy and its role in health promotion, disease prevention and the adoption of healthy lifestyles. This year's theme emphasises preventive and promotive healthcare through appropriate dietary practices, physical activity, yoga, stress management and other evidence-informed naturopathic approaches. It also seeks to strengthen public awareness about obesity prevention and lifestyle-related disorders, encouraging individuals and communities to adopt healthier and more sustainable lifestyles. The observance aligns with the vision of the Hon’ble Prime Minister for a Fit and Healthy India, emphasising preventive healthcare, healthy living and collective responsibility towards public well-being.
Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Ayush and Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, reiterated, “Naturopathy encourages us to recognise the close relationship between lifestyle, nature and overall health. Our emphasis is on strengthening its scientific foundation through credible research, quality education and responsible integration with conventional healthcare. This approach can contribute to preventive healthcare while advancing the vision of a Fit and Healthy India.”
Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, highlighted, “Scientific validation is essential for strengthening the credibility and wider application of naturopathy. Through CCRYN and other institutions, we are encouraging systematic research, clinical evaluation and collaboration so that naturopathic practices can be assessed through appropriate scientific methods and translated into responsible healthcare approaches.”
The Central Council for Research in Yoga and Naturopathy (CCRYN) published Various research papers in peer-reviewed journals during FY 2025–26, while five research councils under the Ministry collectively published 653 papers. The Council also has 22 units across India, reflecting its institutional presence in research, education and outreach.
India's institutional infrastructure has expanded through postgraduate institutes dedicated to Yoga and Naturopathy education and research, along with 200-bed Yoga and Naturopathy hospitals at Jhajjar in Haryana and Nagamangala in Karnataka. The Bachelor of Naturopathy and Yogic Sciences (BNYS) College at Nisarg Gram, National Institute of Naturopathy (NIN), Pune, the first such college established under the Central Government, further strengthens this ecosystem through academic and clinical training, research-based learning and practical exposure in naturopathy and yoga, preparing graduates for careers in healthcare, research, academics and private practice.
The National Institute of Naturopathy (NIN), Pune, has further strengthened its research framework through a dedicated Research Department and an Institutional Ethics Committee registered with the Department of Health Research. Its initiatives include research methodology workshops, Good Clinical Practice training, observational studies, systematic reviews and collaborative research.
The growing research emphasis is particularly relevant as naturopathy promotes healthy dietary practices, physical activity, adequate rest and stress management. These lifestyle measures can support preventive healthcare across different age groups and contribute to greater awareness of lifestyle-related risk factors.
On National Naturopathy Day, the focus remains on strengthening the scientific foundation of naturopathy, expanding institutional capacity and encouraging healthier lifestyles. Through sustained research, quality education and public participation, India aims to further develop a credible and accessible naturopathy ecosystem that complements its wider preventive healthcare efforts and contributes to the vision of ‘Prakrutik Chikitsa, Swasth Bharat’.

subtitle:
Dr. P.K. Mishra calls for linking farmers’ traditional knowledge with scientific research, seed systems and markets

Farmers must be recognised as custodians and innovators of India's agricultural biodiversity: Dr. P.K. Mishra

India's National Genebank is the world's second largest; around 3,000 climate-resilient crop varieties developed: Dr. P.K. Mishra

“An award honours a farmer once; a seed chain, a market and a fair share of benefits sustain the farmer every season”: Dr. P.K. Mishra
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 NOV 2026 4:42PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister, Dr. P.K. Mishra, today called for recognising farmers as custodians and innovators of India's agricultural biodiversity and linking their traditional knowledge with scientific research, seed systems and market opportunities. Addressing the 22nd Foundation Day of the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Authority (PPVFRA) and the Plant Genome Saviour Award Ceremony, Dr. Mishra noted that the occasion marked 25 years of the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Act, 2001.
He said India's rich agricultural biodiversity was vital for developing crops resilient to climate change, water stress, pests and diseases, while preserving traditional knowledge, food cultures and community livelihoods. He highlighted India's 22 agro-biodiversity hotspots and cited Koraput in Odisha, recognised by FAO in 2012 as a Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System, as an example of community-led conservation.
Highlighting India's distinctive framework for farmers' rights, Dr. Mishra said the Act balanced plant breeders' rights with recognition of farmers as conservers, cultivators and developers of plant varieties. Nearly half of the varieties registered under PPVFRA were farmers' varieties. He also emphasised the role of benefit-sharing provisions and the National Gene Fund in ensuring fair returns to communities conserving genetic resources.
Referring to India's scientific capabilities, he noted that the National Genebank at ICAR-NBPGR was the second largest in the world and that around 3,000 climate-resilient crop varieties had been developed under the National Agricultural Research System. He also highlighted the potential of Geographical Indications in creating economic opportunities for distinctive agricultural products.
Dr. Mishra highlighted India's contribution to international efforts on farmers' rights through its engagement with the International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture, the 2022 Governing Body session in New Delhi and the 2023 Global Symposium on Farmers' Rights. He also referred to the Indore Declaration adopted by BRICS Agriculture Ministers and the establishment of a Global Forum on Farmers' Rights in Seed Systems.
Calling for a shift from recognition to empowerment, Dr. Mishra emphasised strengthening community seed banks and field gene banks, connecting traditional knowledge with modern scientific research, and linking farmers' varieties with quality seed systems, Farmer Producer Organisations and wider markets. He called for promoting farmer entrepreneurship and ensuring fair and transparent benefit-sharing so that conservation translated into sustainable economic opportunities.
Concluding his address, Dr. Mishra said farmers must be recognised not merely as participants in India's agricultural transformation but also as contributors and beneficiaries of it.Emphasising the need for sustained economic returns for farmers conserving traditional varieties, he observed: “An award honours a farmer once; a seed chain, a market and a fair share of benefits sustain the farmer every season.” He said safeguarding agricultural diversity was a shared responsibility of farmers, scientists, universities, industry, the State and society, and congratulated the Authority and all award recipients.

content:
The 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026, organised by the India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO), will be held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, from 14 to 27 November 2026. Union Minister of Commerce and Industry, Shri Piyush Goyal, will inaugurate the Fair as the Chief Guest on 13 November 2026.
The inauguration ceremony will also feature an Odissi performance by Padma Shri awardee Guru Madhavi Mudgal and her group.
Themed ‘Vikas aur Virasat’, IITF 2026 will bring together more than 3,500 exhibitors from India and abroad across 17 halls, covering over 1,00,000 square metres of exhibition space. The Fair will witness participation from 32 States and Union Territories and 51 Central Ministries, Government Departments, PSUs and Public Sector Banks. Bihar, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh are the Partner States, while Assam, Delhi, Jharkhand and West Bengal are the Focus States. The participating States and UTs will showcase their regional products, local industries, traditional crafts, culture, tourism potential and development initiatives.
International participation will include 11 countries, with pavilions featuring exhibitors from Thailand, Iran, Ghana, Nepal, Afghanistan, the UAE, Turkey, China, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh, providing opportunities for international business engagement and trade linkages.
Chairman, India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO), Shri Jawed Ashraf, said that IITF 2026 will celebrate India's progress, diversity and heritage, with a special focus on youth through around 600 start-ups at the Hall of Inspiration and district-level crafts, cuisine and culture at the ODOP Pavilion.
Visitors will find country pavilions in Hall 1, Partner and Focus States, Central Ministries, PSUs and Public Sector Banks in Halls 2 to 5, and a wide range of consumer categories across Halls 8 to 14. These will include electronics, consumer durables, textiles, footwear, kitchen equipment, processed food, spices, agricultural produce, handicrafts, home furniture, cosmetics and jewellery.
IITF 2026 will introduce new experiences for businesses and visitors alike. The Hall of Inspiration in Hall 14 will showcase around 600 Indian start-ups across deep-tech, agri-tech, drones, space, healthcare and edtech, providing young enterprises with visibility and opportunities to connect with wider markets.
The One District One Product (ODOP) Pavilion will feature participation from 21 States and showcase signature crafts, cuisine, culture and products from districts across the country, highlighting local enterprise, traditional skills and the artisans behind them.
Playverse@Mandapam will offer an immersive and interactive digital experience combining entertainment and education, designed particularly to engage young visitors and families. Together, these initiatives reflect the spirit of ‘Vikas aur Virasat’, bringing India's technological progress, entrepreneurship and traditional strengths onto one platform.
A world-class food court featuring more than 90 outlets will serve Indian and international cuisines, with an emphasis on food quality, hygiene, zero-waste practices and reduced plastic usage.
Beyond its role as a major trade exhibition, IITF continues to strengthen market access for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), start-ups and small traders by providing opportunities to showcase products, connect with potential buyers and explore new markets. ITPO is also facilitating the participation of Indian start-ups at international platforms such as VivaTech in Paris and the upcoming Singapore FinTech Festival, creating opportunities for global exposure and collaboration. The initiative aims to encourage entrepreneurship across the country, including the growing start-up ecosystem in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities.
Reflecting the growing scale of Bharat Mandapam, the venue will feature LED mesh installations measuring approximately 1,000 square metres each at Hall 1 and Hall 14, alongside plans for around 100 LED screens across the complex, with more than 30 expected to be installed during the Fair. ITPO is also working towards developing Bharat Mandapam as a year-round destination for exhibitions, cultural programmes and public engagement, including a proposed cultural hub with a seating capacity of approximately 2,000.
To ensure a seamless and comfortable experience for visitors, exhibitors, delegates and media representatives, ITPO has put in place a range of dedicated support facilities across the venue. A dedicated Media Lounge will provide workspace for journalists, while a Protocol Lounge will facilitate hospitality for VIPs and dignitaries. Additional arrangements include internal mobility assistance, shuttle services, golf carts, designated cab and parking zones, B2B networking facilities, exhibitor assistance and lost-and-found services.
Food court operations will be subject to round-the-clock monitoring, with prescribed food safety, hygiene and food-handling standards applicable to all outlets, including State-operated stalls. Security arrangements, supported by Delhi Police and ITPO, particularly for the international pavilions in Hall 1, along with medical centres, first-aid facilities and emergency response services, will further strengthen visitor safety and convenience throughout the Fair.
Complementing the exhibition, 87 cultural performances, recitals and shows across seven venues will celebrate India's diversity, spanning classical and folk traditions and featuring acclaimed masters alongside young and upcoming talent. Highlights include The Manganiyar Seduction, Tal Fry, Hariharan & Prithvi Gandharva, Shahzad Ali, Salim–Sulaiman and Ruhaniyat, featuring performers from Nigeria, with tickets available on BookMyShow. Other cultural performances from 19 States and organisations will be free with IITF entry.
The first five days, from 14 to 18 November, will be Business Days reserved for B2B visitors, and the Fair will open to the general public from 19 to 27 November. Fair timings will be from 10:00 AM to 7:30 PM, with general public entry until 5:30 PM. Entry tickets can be booked at booking.indiatradefair.com, through the official IITF 2026 mobile app, or offline at 55 DMRC Metro stations. Season tickets are available for both Business Days and General Days. Senior citizens and persons with disabilities can enter free on General Days with a valid government-issued ID. General visitors can enter through Gate Nos. 3 and 4 on Bhairon Road and Gate Nos. 6 and 10 on Mathura Road.
The IITF 2026 app, available on Google Play and the Apple App Store, offers ticket booking, registration, an interactive venue map with navigation and shuttle routes, a pavilion and exhibitor directory, the cultural events calendar and business networking facilities. ITPO has also coordinated with Delhi Metro and arranged visitor transportation facilities, including shuttle services, designated app-cab and auto pick-up points, parking, wheelchair assistance and visitor support services. The app also provides access to the ITPO helpdesk and one-tap SOS assistance.
The India International Trade Fair, organised annually by ITPO, is one of India's leading multi-product trade exhibitions. It brings together government organisations, industries, businesses, start-ups, MSMEs and artisans from India and abroad, enabling B2B and B2C engagement, trade and investment promotion, and business networking.
For further information and updates, visit the official website of ITPO at
www.itpo.gov.in/iitf

The Controller General of Defence Accounts (CGDA), Ministry of Defence, has rolled out an extensive outreach initiative as part of the Nationwide Digital Life Certificate (DLC) Campaign 5.0. Coordinated by the Department of Pension & Pensioners’ Welfare (DoP&PW), Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, the month-long campaign is being conducted across the country from November 1 to 30, 2026. As on November 11, 2026, over 20.48 lakh defence pensioners have successfully submitted DLCs, the highest contribution among all participating departments.
The initiative aims to facilitate seamless, hassle-free submission of DLCs for defence pensioners and family pensioners through advanced technology-enabled solutions. A key priority is ensuring that elderly, super-senior, and differently-abled pensioners complete their annual identification conveniently without procedural hardships.
Extensive Pan-India Mobilisation
To ensure widespread physical outreach and ground-level support, the Defence Accounts Department (DAD) has mobilised:
194 SPARSH Service Centres (SSCs)
fully equipped to assist pensioners in generating  DLCs and avail SPARSH platform services.
4.63 lakh Common Service Centres (CSCs)
, 13 partner banks / IPPB and 29 nodal officers to facilitate pensioners to generate DLCs.
Around
80 outreach programmes
are being conducted across the country.
Mega Camps
: A Mega Digital Life Certificate Camp to be organised in Kochi on November 23, 2026 offering on-the-spot assistance in generation of DLC.
Promotion of Face Authentication Technology
A focal point of Campaign 5.0 is promoting Aadhaar-based Face Authentication Technology via Jeevan Pramaan portal and mobile application, with more than 80% of the digital life certificates being generated through Face ID. This facility allows pensioners to authenticate their life certificate using a smartphone, eliminating the need for external biometric hardware.
Key advantages include

Submission from Home
: Enables pensioners to generate certificates from the comfort of their homes, cutting down travel time and eliminating physical visits to bank branches or defence offices.
Overcoming Biometric Degradation
: Addresses difficulties faced by super-senior pensioners whose fingerprints have faded with the passage of time and advancing age.
Support for Differently-Abled Veterans
: Provides significant ease of access for pensioners facing reduced mobility.
Digital Self-Reliance
: Encourages pensioners and their families to adopt digital practices, building self-sufficiency for future annual submissions.
Building on Proven Achievements
The Defence Accounts Department has consistently driven high adoption in nationwide digital governance initiatives. During DLC Campaign 4.0 in November 2025, the DAD generated over 20.94 lakh DLCs, through its pan-India network of SPARSH Service Centers, Common Service Centres and partner banks.
Outreach under SPARSH has also expanded significantly, with 35.11 lakh defence pensioners onboarded as of October 2026, supported by 301 SPARSH Outreach Programmes and 204 Raksha Pension Samadhan Aayojans resolving over 8,000 grievances on the spot.
Reiterating its guiding principle ‘Right Pension to the Right Pensioner at the Right Time’, the Defence Accounts Department has urged to all defence pensioners and family pensioners to visit their nearest SPARSH Service Center, banks or one of the 80 outreach programmes during November 2026 to experience a hassle-free, fully digitised life certificate submission process.

content:
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has called upon the Defence Forces to strengthen and sustain both offensive and defensive dimensions of the ‘element of surprise’ to maintain operational readiness against conventional and emerging threats arising from rapid technological advancements and the evolving nature of modern warfare. Addressing the Air Force Commanders’ Conference in New Delhi on November 12, 2026, he emphasised the need to continue bolstering intelligence and surveillance capabilities, enhance integration among systems and identify potential threats before they unfold.
“Our Defence Forces must develop capabilities and methods that leave the adversary with no time to react or recover, while simultaneously ensuring that we are never caught off guard by an unexpected move from the enemy. Surprise can manifest in various forms, both conventional and electronic. Our intelligence and surveillance mechanisms must be further strengthened and operational preparedness enhanced to ensure that our personnel remain alert, agile and equipped to respond effectively to any emerging challenge,” said the Raksha Mantri.
Shri Rajnath Singh asserted that contemporary conflicts are extending beyond traditional battlefields into non-contact domains, with missiles, drones and advanced weapon systems playing a significant role. Referring to the Russia-Ukraine and Israel-Hamas conflicts, he stated that drones and air defence systems have emerged as critical components of modern warfare. He exhorted the Commanders to remain prepared for emerging challenges such as kamikaze drones, surveillance and counter-drone operations.
Raksha Mantri called upon the Indian Air Force (IAF) to develop dedicated doctrines and architectures for emerging domains of warfare, including electronic, cyber and space. He emphasised that enhanced preparedness in these domains would strengthen the ability to address future challenges. “Victory in future conflicts would depend not merely on the number of aircraft, but also on technological sophistication, speed of response and precision of preparations,” he said, urging the Commanders to make these emerging challenges a core priority, with focus on integrating them into institutional thinking, planning and operational processes.
Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted that the Defence Forces are undergoing a transformative phase, encompassing reforms in wide-ranging areas, including organisational structures, jointness & integration, and operational concepts. He added that the changing security environment necessitated continuous adaptation and a forward-looking approach to military preparedness.
Raksha Mantri commended the IAF for effectively implementing its doctrines and operational methods during and after Operation Sindoor, appreciating the professionalism, restraint & judgement demonstrated by the air warriors in successfully executing their assigned tasks. He stated that the lessons learnt during the operation were clearly reflected in the IAF's evolving operational procedures, particularly through the increased emphasis on drones and air defence systems, which are vital to national security. These lessons, he added, are shaping the pace and direction of the transformative changes underway in the Defence Forces.
Highlighting the coordinated and complementary contributions of all the three Services effectively demonstrated during Op Sindoor, Shri Rajnath Singh congratulated the Defence Forces for the synergy and integration. He underlined that jointness and integrated efforts must continue to guide military planning and operational execution.
While appreciating the IAF for enhancing the skills and capabilities of its personnel in keeping with rapid technological advancements, Raksha Mantri urged the Commanders to sustain efforts towards training air warriors in emerging technologies. He underscored the importance of leveraging the technological knowledge and expertise of young recruits, stating that their capabilities could contribute significantly to stronger decision-making and organisational development.
On the Second Tour of Duty for Agniveers, Shri Rajnath Singh stated that the decision was taken following feedback received from the Defence Forces, reiterating the Government's commitment to incorporating the Services’ suggestions into policy decisions. He expressed confidence that the ‘Second Tour of Duty’ initiative would contribute to further bolstering the three Services.
As part of this conference, Raksha Mantri launched a suite of Artificial Intelligence (Al) applications developed in-house by the IAF's Al Centre of Excellence of the Unit for Digitisation, Automation, Artificial Intelligence and Application Networking (UDAAN). The applications will be utilised to automate and expedite tasks across the domains of operations, administration and aerospace safety, and are deployed on the IAF’s secure network. The initiative marks a significant milestone in the IAF's pursuit of technology-driven transformation and enhanced operational capabilities.
The inaugural session was also attended by Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth, Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, Secretary (Defence Production) Shri Sanjeev Kumar, and Secretary (Defence Finance) Shri Vishvajit Sahay. title: DRI busts red sanders smuggling syndicate at Chennai Port; seizes around 13,000 kg red sanders worth Rs. 7.72 crore; three arrested
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 NOV 2026 6:03PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Acting on specific intelligence regarding an attempt by a Chennai-based syndicate to smuggle Red Sanders logs to Malaysia, officers of the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), intercepted an export container at Chennai Port during 9–11 November 2026, before its loading onto the vessel.
The container, declared to contain “Paper Laminate Rolls”, was subjected to detailed examination on 9–10 November 2026. Examination revealed 12.87 metric tonnes of high-grade Red Sanders logs, valued at approximately Rs. 7.72 crore, concealed alongside a small quantity of the declared cargo and gravel stones. The Red Sanders and cover cargo were seized under the provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.
Preliminary investigation revealed that the syndicate had exploited the self-sealing facility available to a manufacturer-exporter. The syndicate arranged an export consignment through the exporter, diverted the container to a private godown and replaced the declared paper laminate rolls with Red Sanders logs before dispatching it for export.
A subsequent search of the godown led to the recovery of the original declared cargo, an industrial weighing scale and traces of Red Sanders, providing further evidence of the modus operandi.
Three key members of the syndicate involved in the smuggling operation have been arrested under the provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.
Red Sanders (Pterocarpus santalinus) is a protected species listed under Appendix II of the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) and Schedule IV of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. Its export from India is prohibited under the Foreign Trade Policy.
The operation highlights the misuse of legitimate export channels and trade facilitation measures for organised wildlife trafficking. DRI remains committed to dismantling such smuggling networks and protecting India’s rich biodiversity through intelligence-led enforcement.

title: DRI seizes 22 kg cocaine from passenger arriving from Sierra Leone in New Delhi
subtitle: Foreign female passenger arrested for attempting to smuggle contraband under guise of diplomatic persona
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 NOV 2026 5:49PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a major crackdown on international drug syndicates, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has intercepted a foreign female passenger arriving from Sierra Leone and seized 22 kg (net) of cocaine
from her possession. The seized narcotics are estimated to have a value of several crores of rupees in the illicit international market.
The operation exposed a sophisticated and brazen modus operandi involving the use of forged diplomatic credentials to bypass airport security.
The passenger claimed to be a diplomatic courier and was carrying a large briefcase-type box bearing markings such as “Diplomatic Mail” and “Do Not Open Without Authority”. She also produced apparently forged documents claiming that the consignment belonged to a United Nations diplomatic courier, evidently to evade scrutiny.
Acting on the intelligence input, DRI officers conducted a thorough examination of the briefcase in accordance with due procedure. The examination resulted in the recovery of 22 packets, concealed within multiple layers of plastic wrapping. The white, brick-shaped substance recovered from the packets tested positive for cocaine during field testing.
The entire contraband, comprising 22 packets of cocaine, was seized under the provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985. The passenger was arrested under the provisions of the NDPS Act, 1985 and produced before the competent court.
The DRI remains firmly committed to dismantling novel trafficking routes, leveraging intelligence-led enforcement, and dismantling international syndicates attempting to exploit institutional privileges for illicit trade.

title: India Makes Major Strides Towards TB Elimination: 38% Decline in TB Mortality, 94% Treatment Success Rate
subtitle:
WHO Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 Highlights India's Remarkable Progress in Reducing TB Deaths and Strengthening Treatment Outcomes

India Records Its Highest-Ever Reduction of 38% in TB Mortality, Outperforming Global Decline of 35%

PM Modi's Vision of TB-Mukt Bharat Drives Nationwide Transformation Through Early Detection, Advanced Diagnostics, Nutritional Support and Jan Bhagidari

TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Covers Over 25 Crore People; More Than 11 Crore Chest X-Rays and 3 Crore Molecular Tests Conducted

48.64 Lakh TB Cases Detected, Including 14.97 Lakh Asymptomatic Cases, Through Intensified Screening

96% of TB Programme Funding Requirements Met Through Domestic Resources, Reflecting India's Strong Commitment to TB Elimination
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 NOV 2026 8:40PM by PIB Delhi
content:
India has achieved a significant milestone in its fight against tuberculosis (TB), recording a
38% reduction in TB mortality since 2015, compared to a global decline of 35%, alongside an impressive 94% treatment success rate among patients with drug-susceptible TB.
These achievements, highlighted in the World Health Organization's (WHO)
Global Tuberculosis Report 2026
, released on 12th November 2026, reflect India's sustained progress towards eliminating TB through early detection, timely treatment, technological innovation and comprehensive patient care.
India's reduction in TB mortality
highlights the country's strong performance in reducing TB-related deaths. The progress reflects the impact of intensified interventions under the National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP), including proactive case finding including use of AI enabled X-rays, rapid diagnostics, prompt treatment initiation, differentiated TB care, and nutritional support through the Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana and Ni-kshay Mitra initiative. These interventions were supported by AI tools for identification of hotspots, prediction of high-risk TB cases prone for adverse outcomes, Khushi - AI Chatbot & Avatar Videobot, etc.
The high
treatment success rate of 94%
further demonstrates the effectiveness of India's patient-centred approach, strengthened treatment delivery and sustained support for people affected by TB.
Under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India's fight against TB has evolved into a nationwide Jan Andolan, bringing together government institutions, healthcare professionals, communities and citizens in pursuit of a TB-Mukt Bharat. Guided by the Prime Minister's emphasis on Jan Bhagidari, the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan has accelerated community-based screening, AI-enabled chest X-rays, rapid molecular diagnostics, TB preventive treatment and nutritional support, taking essential services closer to vulnerable populations.
India's commitment is further reflected in
96% of TB programme funding requirements being met through domestic resources
, demonstrating sustained national investment, strong political commitment and a whole-of-government, whole-of-society approach to TB elimination.
TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan: Over 25 Crore People Brought Under Intensified Screening
The TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan has emerged as a major driver of India's accelerated TB elimination efforts, transforming the approach to TB detection through proactive screening, technology-enabled diagnostics and community outreach.
The first intensified 100-day campaign, launched on 7 December 2024 across 347 high-priority districts in 33 States and Union Territories, was subsequently expanded nationwide to strengthen early detection, particularly among vulnerable and high-risk populations. Building upon the learnings and momentum generated, another intensified 100 Days campaign was launched by the Government on 24th March 2026, focussing on TB screening in 1.58 lakh high risk villages & wards, congregate settings & vulnerable population.
Between 7 December 2024 and 8th November 2026, the Abhiyaan achieved significant progress:
Over 25 crore individuals
identified and brought within the ambit of TB screening activities.
More than 11 crore chest X-rays
conducted to strengthen early detection.
Over 3 crore nucleic acid amplification tests (NAAT)
conducted for rapid and accurate diagnosis.
48.64 lakh new TB cases
identified, including
14.97 lakh asymptomatic cases
.
The detection of nearly 15 lakh asymptomatic cases is particularly significant, demonstrating the effectiveness of proactive screening in identifying individuals who might otherwise remain undiagnosed. Early identification facilitates timely treatment and provides opportunities to reduce TB transmission and prevent severe disease.
The Abhiyaan also focuses on prompt treatment initiation, differentiated patient care, nutritional assistance and continued community-based support to improve treatment outcomes. With these efforts, 67933 Panchayats have been declared TB Free in 2025.
Technology and Innovation Transforming TB Diagnosis and Care
India is increasingly leveraging advanced technologies to make TB screening and diagnosis faster, more accurate and accessible.
The deployment of
portable AI-enabled digital X-rays
, expansion of rapid molecular diagnostic technologies, including NAAT, and strengthening of diagnostic infrastructure have significantly enhanced the programme's ability to reach populations across diverse geographical and social settings.
The
Ni-kshay digital platform
supports patient tracking, treatment monitoring and programme management, strengthening continuity of care and timely interventions.
The integration of TB screening with the identification and management of diabetes, undernutrition and other comorbidities is further enabling comprehensive and patient-centred treatment.
Nutritional support remains a key pillar of India's TB response. Through the
Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana
, eligible patients receive financial assistance towards nutritional requirements during treatment, while the
Ni-kshay Mitra initiative
mobilises individuals, institutions and organisations to provide nutritional and psychosocial support.
These interventions, together with improved diagnostics and patient follow-up, are contributing to stronger treatment outcomes and reduced TB mortality.
India's TB Progress Backed by Robust Scientific Surveillance and Evidence
India's achievements are also supported by strengthened epidemiological surveillance, scientific research and evidence-based TB estimation.
The WHO Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 has incorporated evidence from multiple complementary sources, including the Registrar General of India's Sample Registration System (RGI/SRS), community-based verbal autopsy assessments and programme data from the Ni-kshay portal, to strengthen TB mortality estimation.
Based on these assessments, the
report documents a 38% reduction in India's estimated TB mortality with the rate decreasing from 28 per lakh of the population in 2015 to 18 per lakh of the population in 2025.
The Indian Council of Medical Research–National Institute for Research in Tuberculosis (ICMR-NIRT) conducted a nationally representative TB prevalence survey in 2025, which has been shared with WHO & is under technical discussions, following which WHO will publish an updated country profile for India.
Jan Bhagidari: Making TB Elimination a People's Movement
A defining feature of India's TB elimination efforts has been the mobilisation of communities and institutions as active partners in the national mission.
The participation of Panchayati Raj Institutions, urban local bodies, elected representatives, civil society organisations, private healthcare providers, corporate partners and community leaders has strengthened awareness, screening, nutritional assistance and patient support at the grassroots level.
The
Ni-kshay Mitra initiative
has further encouraged citizens and institutions to directly contribute to the recovery and well-being of people undergoing TB treatment, reinforcing the spirit of collective responsibility.
Building on this momentum, the
JOSH Teams initiative
is bringing greater youth participation into the TB elimination movement. Teams are being constituted at block and ward levels, led by designated Class-I officers and supported by five NCC cadets and five MY Bharat volunteers.
Through awareness generation, community outreach and mobilisation, JOSH Teams are helping strengthen grassroots participation and advance the vision of a TB-Mukt Bharat.
Sustaining the Momentum Towards a TB-Mukt Bharat
The achievements highlighted in the WHO Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 reflect India's sustained investments in public health, technological innovation, scientific surveillance and community-driven interventions.
The 38% decline in TB mortality, 94% treatment success rate and unprecedented scale of screening under the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan mark important progress in India's journey towards TB elimination.
The Government will continue to build on these gains through intensified screening, expanded access to quality diagnostics, prompt and effective treatment, TB preventive treatment, nutritional assistance and deeper community engagement.
Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India remains firmly committed to accelerating progress towards global TB targets and realising the vision of a
TB-Mukt Bharat
, working in close collaboration with WHO, research institutions, States and Union Territories, development partners and communities.
TB Harega, Desh Jeetega!

title: Union Jal Shakti Minister Shri C. R. Paatil Addresses First Regional Conference on JJM 2.0 at Tiruchirappalli
subtitle:
Seven Southern States and Union Territories deliberate on accelerating implementation and ensuring long-term functionality of rural drinking water supply schemes

Inter-ministerial convergence, source sustainability, institutional strengthening and Gram Panchayat-led water governance emerge as key priorities
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 NOV 2026 7:53PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Shri C. R. Paatil, Hon’ble Union Minister of Jal Shakti, addressed the first Regional Conference on Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0, organised by the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, in collaboration with the Government of Tamil Nadu. The two-day conference, being held on 12–13 November 2026, brings together senior officials and representatives from seven southern States and Union Territories namely, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Keralam, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Puducherry and Lakshadweep  to review progress, address challenges and strengthen sustainable rural drinking water services. implementation
Chairing the Ministerial Session at the Conference,
Hon’ble Union Minister of Jal Shakti
, recalled the transformative vision of the Hon’ble Prime Minister behind the launch of Jal Jeevan Mission in 2019, aimed at ensuring access to tap water for every rural household. He highlighted the remarkable progress achieved under the Mission, with household tap water connections reaching approximately 16 crore rural households, significantly improving the lives of rural communities, particularly women.
The Union Minister noted that the Regional Conference was being organised as a
follow-up to the Departmental Summit on Water held on 1–2 September 2026
, to translate the deliberations and decisions of the Summit into concrete action at the State, district and village levels. He emphasised that the remaining works must be completed within the approved Mission timeline of December 2028 and appealed to States to make concerted efforts towards completing them by December 2027, wherever feasible.
Hon’ble Minister underscored that JJM 2.0 represents a transition from infrastructure creation to assured and sustainable drinking water service delivery. He stressed the need for States to operationalise the prescribed structural reforms, particularly those relating to operation and maintenance (O&M), institutional accountability and long-term functionality of rural water supply systems. He reiterated the Government of India's commitment to providing financial support for eligible works, subject to fulfilment of the prescribed reform conditions, and urged States to accelerate implementation and effective utilisation of available resources.
Emphasising the importance of water security, the Union Minister called for greater attention to groundwater recharge, rainwater harvesting and community-led water conservation. Referring to
Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari
, he highlighted the potential of decentralised water conservation structures and urged States to strengthen convergence among departments and actively involve communities in source sustainability measures. He also encouraged participating States to exchange successful practices and adopt practical solutions to overcome implementation challenges.
Shri Thiru N. Anand, Hon’ble Minister, Rural Development and Panchayati Raj,  and Water Resources in the Government of Tamil Nadu
, highlighted the State's progress in expanding rural household tap water connections and strengthening drinking water infrastructure through combined water supply schemes and improvement of existing systems. He outlined initiatives relating to O&M, periodic cleaning of overhead tanks, community-based water quality testing, collection of water service charges and district-level monitoring of drinking water services. He reaffirmed Tamil Nadu's commitment to JJM 2.0 and emphasised continued Centre–State cooperation for completing the remaining works and sustaining drinking water services.
Shri Ashok K. K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS
, stated that the Tiruchirappalli conference was the first in a series of five regional conferences aimed at translating the outcomes of the Department al Summit on Water held in September 2026 into actionable measures. He emphasised source sustainability, effective O&M arrangements, financial sustainability, skilled local workforce and strengthened Gram Panchayat-led governance as key priorities. He also highlighted the importance of digital platforms, including Sujalam Bharat, and inter-ministerial convergence to support sustainable service delivery.
Shri Kamal Kishore Soan,
Additional Secretary and Mission Director, NJJM, during his interactions across various presentations, emphasised the need to translate reforms into effective field-level implementation and strengthen interdepartmental coordination among Rural Development, Panchayati Raj and Rural Water Supply Departments.
He highlighted the need for regular assessment of drinking water sources, effective utilisation of Finance Commission grants, strengthening Gram Panchayat own-source revenue and ensuring sustainable financing for operation and maintenance.
During the Ministerial Session,
Shri D. Senthil Pandiyan, Joint Secretary, DDWS,
apprised the Hon’ble Union Minister on the objectives and key deliberations of the Regional Conference. He highlighted the importance of regional conferences as platforms for mutual learning, sharing of best practices and strengthening coordination among States/UTs. Referring to the historical significance of the Kallanai Dam and the Cauvery water management system, he emphasised community ownership, effective operation and maintenance, and interdepartmental convergence for ensuring sustainable rural drinking water services under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0.
The conference commenced with a welcome address by
Shri Dinesh Ponraj Oliver,
Mission Director, JJM, Tamil Nadu
. Senior officials of the Government of Tamil Nadu and representatives of participating States and Union Territories also attended the deliberations.
Shri Hari Narayan Murugun, Director, DDWS
, presented the vision and key structural reforms under JJM 2.0 and reviewed the progress of participating States and Union Territories on various reform parameters. The presentation highlighted institutional strengthening, service utility arrangements, source sustainability, water quality governance, digital monitoring, capacity building and skilled human resources.
The
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
, represented by Dr. M Jayaprakashan, Regional Director, RDSDE, highlighted the importance of developing a skilled local workforce for the operation and maintenance of rural drinking water systems, including training and certification of village-level functionaries.
Shri Y. K. Singh, Director, DDWS
, highlighted convergence opportunities with major tribal development initiatives, including
PM-JANMAN
and
Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DA-JGUA)
, to address drinking water requirements in tribal and particularly vulnerable tribal group habitations.
The
Ministry of Rural Development
, represented by Ms. Deeksha Supyaal Bisht, Assistant Commissioner, VB-G RAM G
and Shri Gauri Shankar, Project Officer, MoRD
, presented opportunities for convergence under VB-G RAM G for water conservation, groundwater recharge, source sustainability and eligible maintenance-related interventions.
Shri Vipul Ujwal, Director, Ministry of Panchayati Raj
, highlighted the central role of Gram Panchayats in sustaining rural drinking water services, with particular emphasis on O&M financing, integration of drinking water requirements into Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs) and utilisation of Finance Commission grants. The discussions also emphasised convergence of
capacity-building modules developed under JJM 2.0 with the training framework of Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA)
