title: Proposed Rent a Cab reforms to expand business opportunities and improve passenger services
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 NOV 2026 9:05PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has proposed reforms to make cab rental businesses easier to start and operate, expand rental choices and strengthen passenger safety. The proposed framework combines simpler procedures with better customer support.
Key provisions
•
Easier entry and more choice:
Operators may offer cabs with or without drivers. The minimum fleet falls from 50 to 5, with at least 2 cabs per place of operation. The requirement for branches in five tourist cities is removed.
•
One electronic licence:
A single licence, valid across the State or UT for a uniform fee, replaces separate main and branch licences. Approved places of operation may include airports, stations and bus terminals.
•
Timely approvals:
Licence grants and renewals have a proposed 60-day timeline. Adding or removing cabs or places of operation has a 30-day deemed-approval mechanism.
•
Less paperwork:
Electronic VAHAN registers and automatic data retrieval simplify compliance.
•
Safer journeys:
Cabs must have location tracking, child restraint systems (optional) and first-aid kits. Operators must provide a website, 24-hour grievance support, emergency repairs and towing.
•
Driver welfare and accountability:
Operator-provided drivers would require police verification, with welfare under the Code on Social Security, 2020. Specified serious offences involving a cab or operator-provided driver will reduce operator’s licence validity.
•
Fairer enforcement and easier appeals:
Operators get time to correct non-material violations before suspension or revocation is considered. An appellate mechanism with electronic hearings is also introduced.
Intended impact
Ease of Living:
Wider rental choices, safety equipment and round-the-clock grievance support will benefit renters.
Ease of Doing Business:
Lower entry barriers and simpler licensing will support smaller businesses and employment opportunities.
Stakeholders affected
Renters, operators, drivers and State and UT transport authorities.
Implementation requirements
State and UT oversight, electronic licensing and VAHAN records will support implementation.

content:
The Indian National Science Academy (INSA), an institution of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), actively participated in the S20 2026 process and endorsed the Joint S20 Statement, released by the science academies of the G20 countries, on November 10, 2026, under the leadership of the U.S. National Academy of Sciences (NAS), as part of the Science20 (S20) engagement process.
Through its endorsement of the Joint Statement, which highlights opportunities for governments to harness advanced technologies to strengthen preparedness and response to natural hazards and disasters, INSA reaffirmed its commitment to promoting science-based approaches to address global challenges.
The Statement, developed through consultations and contributions from science academies across G20 nations, is intended to inform discussions within their respective governments. It will also be presented to the G20 ahead of the G20 Summit scheduled to be held in Miami, Florida, in December 2026.
Natural hazards such as heavy rainfall, earthquakes, droughts, wildfires, and extreme heat and cold events are increasingly posing significant challenges to populations, ecosystems and economies. The Statement highlights the potential of emerging technologies, including Earth observation, remote sensing, early warning systems, digital twins, drone technologies and artificial intelligence, to improve decision-making and strengthen disaster preparedness and resilience.
It also recognises that the effective application of these technologies depends on addressing gaps in data availability, infrastructure, technical capacity and institutional coordination, while ensuring equitable access and readiness for deployment.
The Joint S20 Statement identifies five key areas for action. These include strengthening data collection and understanding of risk, enabling safe, secure and equitable access to data and technology, building local skills and capacity and designing context-specific solutions, strengthening human decision-making and governance, and advancing international and cross-sector collaboration.
The Statement underscores that technology should enhance, rather than replace, human expertise and that effective disaster resilience requires locally relevant solutions supported by strong scientific collaboration and institutional partnerships.
As India's national science academy, INSA will endeavour to bring the recommendations of the Statement to the attention of relevant national stakeholders and facilitate engagement among scientific experts, research institutions and government agencies. Through its national and international networks, INSA will continue to encourage interdisciplinary research, knowledge exchange and collaboration in areas relevant to disaster preparedness and resilience.
The S20 2026 process has provided an important platform for science academies across G20 nations to exchange perspectives and contribute collectively to addressing a shared global challenge. INSA looks forward to continuing this engagement under the leadership of the Royal Society in 2027.
KEY AREAS OF ACTION
Strengthening data collection and understanding of risk
: Improving observation systems and the availability of reliable data on hazards, exposure and vulnerability to support preparedness, response and recovery.
Enabling safe, secure and equitable access to data and technology
: Promoting data sharing, common standards, interoperability and resilient systems, while respecting national responsibilities for data governance, safety, security and privacy.
Building local skills and capacity and designing context-specific solutions
: Investing in education, workforce development, training and community engagement to ensure that technologies are adapted to local needs and can be effectively sustained.
Strengthening human decision-making and governance
: Ensuring that advanced technologies complement human expertise through appropriate oversight, local validation, transparency, accountability and effective communication of risks.
Advancing international and cross-sector collaboration
: Encouraging sustained partnerships among governments, academia, industry, civil society, communities and international organisations, with an emphasis on co-producing knowledge and technology.

title: TDB-DST signs agreement with Astrome for ₹64.05 crore RDI support to develop sovereign space-based AI-ELINT constellation
subtitle: Project to advance indigenous electronic intelligence, AI-based ground processing and inter-satellite communication technologies towards TRL-9
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 NOV 2026 12:56PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a significant step towards strengthening India's indigenous space-based intelligence and advanced satellite technology capabilities, the Technology Development Board (TDB), Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, has signed an agreement with M/s Astrome Technologies Pvt Ltd, Bengaluru, Karnataka for financial support of ₹64.05 crore under the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund. The project, with a total project cost of ₹128.11 crore, aims to develop a sovereign space-based Artificial Intelligence-enabled Electronic Intelligence (AI-ELINT) constellation for national security applications. The programme seeks to advance critical technologies from Technology Readiness Level (TRL)-4 to TRL-9, with financial support being provided through Optionally Convertible Debt (OCD).
As the strategic importance of space-based systems continues to grow, the ability to develop and deploy indigenous technologies for intelligence gathering, communication and data processing has become increasingly important. Space-based constellations can provide persistent coverage over large geographical areas, while advances in artificial intelligence are enabling faster processing and interpretation of complex data. Astrome's project seeks to address this emerging technology requirement through the development of an integrated AI-ELINT satellite constellation. The programme brings together three key technology components: an Electronic Intelligence (ELINT) payload, AI-based ground processing software, and      inter-satellite communication links.
The project envisages the development and progressive deployment of AI-ELINT microsatellites in the 50 kg class, designed to operate as part of a constellation architecture. The proposed system aims to provide enhanced coverage and increased observation frequency, supporting persistent surveillance      of identified areas of interest. The ELINT payload forms a key component of the proposed system and is intended to support the detection and analysis of signals across a broad frequency range. Complementing the satellite hardware, the AI-based ground processing software is designed to enable the efficient processing and analysis of information generated by the constellation.
The project also includes the development of an inter-satellite communication link, an important capability for enabling satellites within a constellation to exchange information and operate as an integrated network. The proposed constellation architecture is designed around satellites operating in a low Earth orbit, with an objective of progressively increasing coverage and revisit capability as additional satellites are deployed. The programme will undertake technology development, engineering, integration, testing and validation activities required to advance the core systems towards TRL-9.
The project falls under the Deep Technology sector, with Space Technology as its sub-sector. It represents the convergence of several frontier technologies—satellite engineering, electronic intelligence, artificial intelligence and secure space-based communications.
Shri Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Secretary, Technology Development Board, said,
“India's growing capabilities in space technology are creating new opportunities to develop advanced systems that combine indigenous engineering with artificial intelligence and next-generation communications. Building such complex technology platforms requires sustained innovation, rigorous validation and long-term investment. Through the RDI Fund, TDB is supporting Indian enterprises working on frontier technologies that can strengthen the country's strategic technology capabilities. The project with Astrome reflects the potential of India's deep-tech ecosystem to develop sophisticated space-based solutions for emerging national requirements.”
An authorised representative of Astrome Technologies said,
“The support from TDB under the RDI Fund will help us accelerate the development and integration of critical technologies for our AI-enabled space-based intelligence programme. By bringing together indigenous ELINT payloads, AI-based data processing and inter-satellite communications, we aim to develop an integrated constellation capability that can address emerging requirements in the space and national security domains. This partnership will support our efforts to advance these technologies towards TRL-9.”

title: From Risk to Respect

content:
The journey of the sanitation worker from Puducherry, Mr Muthuvel
(name changed)
highlights how NAMASTE Scheme has contributed to improved workplace safety, livelihood security and social recognition.
Through initiatives such as NAMASTE, the Government of India continues to reaffirm its commitment to protecting, respecting and empowering sanitation workers who play an indispensable role in maintaining public health and cleanliness across the country.
The National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, continues to strengthen occupational safety, dignity and livelihood opportunities for sanitation workers across the country.
Demonstrating the positive impact of the Scheme,
Mr Muthuvel,
a 58-year-old sanitation worker from Oulgaret Municipality, Puducherry
, has experienced significant improvements in his working conditions, health and financial stability following the provision of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) and occupational safety orientation under the initiative.
Belonging to the Other Backward Classes (OBC) community, the beneficiary has been engaged in sewer line cleaning for more than ten years. Having studied up to Class 5, he relied on his occupation to support a family of four, earning approximately ₹9,000–10,000 per month.
Despite his dedication to providing essential sanitation services, the absence of adequate protective equipment exposed him to hazardous waste, harmful gases and other occupational health risks. Frequent health complications and associated medical expenses further affected his ability to maintain regular employment and financial stability.
The challenges extended beyond occupational hazards and economic difficulties. Social stigma associated with sanitation work also affected his professional recognition and sense of dignity. With limited access to essential safety resources, he aspired to secure healthier working conditions, reduce occupational risks and provide greater financial security for his family.
A significant turning point came in 2025 when he was identified as a beneficiary under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme. Through the intervention, he received a comprehensive Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) kit comprising protective gloves, gumboots, overalls, a face mask and a safety helmet. He was also provided orientation on safe sanitation practices, appropriate use of protective equipment and measures to prevent occupational hazards.
The support brought a meaningful improvement in his everyday working conditions. With access to protective equipment and increased awareness of workplace safety, he became better equipped to perform his duties while reducing direct exposure to hazardous substances. The adoption of safer working practices contributed to fewer health complications, improved attendance and greater consistency in his professional responsibilities.
The positive impact of the intervention was also reflected in his financial circumstances. His monthly earnings, which previously ranged between ₹9,000 and ₹10,000, increased to approximately ₹13,000–14,000. Improved health and more regular attendance enabled him to maintain greater work continuity and contribute more consistently to his family's financial needs. The increase in earnings also helped strengthen household financial stability and reduce the burden associated with recurring medical expenses.
Beyond the improvements in occupational safety and income, the intervention contributed to strengthening his confidence and professional dignity. Access to protective equipment and institutional support reinforced the importance of recognising sanitation workers as essential contributors to public health and community well-being. title: Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Reaches Over 35.88 Crore People; Over 14.35 Crore Youth, 11.33 Crore Women Reached Through Nationwide Awareness Campaign
subtitle:
More Than 2 Lakh Citizens Enrolled as Nasha Mukti Mitr

Persons Seeking Treatment and Counselling Increase from 2.08 Lakh in 2020-21 to Over 9.11 Lakh in 2025-26

Total Number Of District De-Addiction Centres In The Country Is 198 As On Date
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 NOV 2026 4:13PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA), launched by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment on 15 August 2020, has evolved into a nationwide people's movement against substance abuse, reaching over
35.88 crore people
across the country as on 12 November 2026.
The campaign has connected with more than
14.35 crore youth and 11.33 crore women
, reflecting its expanding outreach among key sections of society. More than
2 lakh citizens have also enrolled as Nasha Mukti Mitr
, strengthening community participation in the collective effort to build a drug-free India.
A Senior Official in the Ministry said the Abhiyaan was initially launched in 272 districts identified as particularly vulnerable to substance use, that was subsequently expanded to 372 districts in August 2022 and extended to all districts of the country with effect from 15 August 2023.
He said over the past six years, NMBA has evolved from an initiative driven by institutional participation into a community-led movement, with States, districts, educational institutions, civil society organisations and local stakeholders actively contributing to its implementation.
The Official said the Campaign has reached
over 35.88 crore people as on date
, marking a significant expansion from approximately 1.4 crore people reached in 2021. Its growing footprint reflects sustained efforts towards awareness generation, community mobilisation and encouraging citizens to actively participate in the movement against substance abuse, he further said.
The Official noted that more than
34.07 lakh awareness activities have been conducted in educational institutions
, engaging students and young people in discussions on the harmful consequences of substance use.
These activities aim to promote informed choices, encourage healthy lifestyles and strengthen awareness about substance abuse prevention among the younger generation, he added.
He said the NMBA’s expansion is rooted in the need to address substance dependence as a complex psycho-social and medical challenge affecting individuals, families and communities.
The Official informed the first National Survey on the Extent and Pattern of Substance Use in India, conducted in 2018, highlighted the scale of the challenge, indicating that more than 7 crore people in the country were affected by substance use disorders, including nearly 1.2 crore children and 58 lakh women.
Recognising the need for a comprehensive and sustained response, the Ministry launched NMBA as the flagship awareness initiative under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR), which focuses on prevention, treatment and rehabilitation, the Official said.
Alongside awareness generation, the Ministry has strengthened the treatment and counselling ecosystem under NAPDDR, the Official noted.
Emphasizing that the expansion of these services highlights the importance of accessible treatment, timely intervention and sustained rehabilitation in addressing substance dependence, the Official said the number of persons seeking treatment and counselling has increased from
2.08 lakh in 2020-21 to over 9.11 lakh in 2025-26
, reflecting the growing reach and utilisation of support services. The total number of
District De-Addiction Centres in the country is now 198 as on date,
he added.
The Official further said a key component of NMBA is the
Nasha Mukti Mitr
initiative, which encourages citizens to become active participants in the movement against substance abuse.
With more than
2 lakh citizens enrolled as Nasha Mukti Mitr as on 12 November 2026
, the initiative is fostering a network of community volunteers who contribute to awareness generation, encourage individuals to seek assistance and support the creation of drug-free communities, he added.
Through sustained awareness campaigns, strengthened treatment and rehabilitation services and active citizen participation, the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan continues to advance the vision of a healthier, informed and drug-free society.

title: 2nd Edition of the National Tribal Literary Festival 2026 begins in New Delhi: “From Oral Tradition to Contemporary Tribal Literature
subtitle:
“Preserving tribal languages and oral traditions is central to building Viksit Bharat 2047.” – Union Minister of Tribal Affairs

Two-day festival organised by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs to celebrate Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas Pakhwada

Tribal writers, poets, researchers and language experts from across the country to share their works and ideas

Day 1 sessions on tribal literature, a poets’ meet and tribal folklore focused on living tribal values, community consent in documenting cultural heritage, linking state tribal portals and digitising archival holdings
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 NOV 2026 7:57PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Under the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister, the Union Cabinet declared 15th November, the birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda, as Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, to celebrate the rich tribal heritage and bring the contributions of tribal heroes into the national consciousness. Carrying forward this vision, the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Government of India, inaugurated the second edition of the two-day National Tribal Literary Festival today at the India Habitat Centre, New Delhi. Held on the occasion of Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas Pakhwada, the festival celebrates tribal literature, languages, and oral traditions under the inspiring guidance of the Hon’ble Prime Minister. Bringing together tribal writers, poets, researchers and language experts, the festival celebrates the evolution of tribal expression from oral tradition to contemporary literature. In line with the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s mantra of “Virasat bhi, Vikas bhi,” it reaffirms the vision of a Viksit Bharat 2047 that draws strength from its heritage and ensures that tribal languages and knowledge systems are preserved, promoted and woven into the national mainstream.
The festival was inaugurated by the Hon’ble Union Minister of Tribal Affairs, Shri Jual Oram, along with the Hon’ble Minister of State for Tribal Affairs, Shri Durgadas Uikey, the Hon’ble Member of NITI Aayog, Dr. Joram Aniya, Padma Shri Shri Chamu Krishna Shastry, Chairman, Bharatiya Bhasha Samiti, Smt. Ranjana Chopra, Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, and Shri Anant Prakash Pandey, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, by lighting the ceremonial lamp. Tribal writers, researchers and language experts from across the country were present.
Welcoming the dignitaries, tribal writers and experts, the Joint Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs,
Shri Anant Prakash Pandey
, said that the knowledge and traditions of tribal communities must be given national recognition, and that new and young tribal writers have to act as a bridge in translating the rich oral traditions of their communities into written literature, carrying the wisdom of their ancestors to future generations and to the wider nation.
In her opening remarks, the Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs,
Smt. Ranjana Chopra
, said that the festival gives tribal writers and publishers a platform and creates an opportunity for dialogue between senior and young writers. She stressed the importance of preserving the languages and cultural traditions of tribal communities in the country and said that oral traditions must be documented before they disappear. She said the festival aims to give tribal heritage national recognition and secure it for future generations. Noting that this is the second edition of the National Tribal Literary Festival, she said that this will continue as an annual feature in all the Pakhwada periods to come.
Padma Shri Shri Chamu Krishna Shastry, Chairman, Bharatiya Bhasha Samiti,
said that
a nation’s awakening rests on knowledge (Gyana Shakti), action (Kriya Shakti) and willpower (Iccha Shakti).
He said that with willpower, the nation can be awakened to build a grand, prosperous and united India. He stressed on unity in diversity and how language can strengthen national integrity.
Dr. Joram Aniya, Hon’ble Member, NITI Aayog,
describing the festival as a historic gathering celebrating India’s self-respect, ancient traditions and tribal pride, paid homage to Bhagwan Birsa Munda and said his Ulgulan was a struggle to protect tribal culture, language, traditions and identity. She said, “
The real and living literature of India is not found only in books, but resides in the hearts of the people in the form of folk songs, lullabies and stories of our tribal societies
.” She complimented the Ministry of Tribal Affairs for curating such a platform for the documentation of tribal literature.
Shri Durgadas Uikey, Hon’ble Minister of State for Tribal Affairs,
expressed gratitude for the Hon’ble Prime Minister’s visionary leadership in honouring tribal heritage, saying,
“
The Hon’ble Prime Minister has taken the historic initiative of celebrating the birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda as Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas. It is a resolve to connect the country’s tribal heroes, freedom fighters, social reformers and their glorious heritage with the national consciousness
.”
He presented a ten-point (Das Bindu) framework on the essence of tribal oral traditions, covering folktales, folk songs, heroic sagas, myths, proverbs, riddles, rituals and prayers.
Shri Jual Oram, Hon’ble Union Minister of Tribal Affairs,
said that systematic documentation of the literature, folk songs, folktales and oral traditions of tribal languages is essential for their preservation, and that this effort must include not only writers but also lyricists, musicians, folk artists and digital content creators. Noting that many tribal languages have no script and some dialects are on the verge of extinction, he said the absence of a script must not become a barrier, and that oral traditions can be preserved through available Indian languages. He informed that the Ministry will collaborate with the Sahitya Akademi and other organisations working in this field to promote and preserve tribal literature
The first session, “Tribal Literature: From Community Memory to Contemporary Expression”, explored tribal literature as a continuum encompassing oral traditions, cultural memory and contemporary literary creativity. The session was moderated by Prof. Anil Kumar Boro, with Ms. K. Vasamalli, Dr. Damayanti Beshra and Dr. Dharmendra Pare as discussants.
Ms. K. Vasamalli
, representing the Toda community of the Nilgiris, said that without language, a community’s traditions and culture cannot develop. She spoke of her efforts to document the endangered Toda language, which has only about 2,000 speakers, through radio recordings, her published work and a 5,700-word dictionary created using the International Phonetic Alphabet and modified Tamil script. Highlighting the close bond between the Toda people and nature, she said the community does not practise idol worship, and that for them
“the mountains are the temple of the gods.”
She also shared ecological markers embedded in Toda culture, including sacred mountains and rivers and the reverence for native flora used by priests and in clan naming.
Prof. Anil Kumar Boro
, reflecting on concerns about the erosion of traditional values due to modernisation and growing individualism, cited the example of the Mizo people in Aizawl, who maintain strict self-discipline even in city traffic. He said,
“We may be following a modern urbanised way of life, but still we can follow the values that our tribal forefathers had been following and preserving.”
Dr. Dharmendra Pare
said that while memories may fade, knowledge, awareness, conduct and traditions are never destroyed. He noted that the unlettered wisdom once shared in fields and homes is being replaced by screens, and illustrated the essence of tribal consciousness through a festival in which honey is shared by the entire community rather than consumed individually, a Gond story of siblings who turned away from a city market because there was no place for their gods, and the ethical hunting practices of the Baiga and Pardhi communities, who do not hunt pregnant birds. He said true preservation lies in understanding and living these values, and not merely in compiling dictionaries.
The second session, “The Joy of Life: Tribal Poets’ Meet”, was held in two parts, with poetry readings by poets from different tribal languages. The session was moderated by Prof. Kanji Patel. Dr. Rekha Kharadi, Dr. Jitendrabhai Vajirsing Vasava, Ms. Yashoda Murmu, Dr. Jomyir Jini, Prof. Snehlata Negi and Ms. Parwati Tirkey presented their poems.
The third session, “Tribal Folklore: Songs, Myths, Tales, Proverbs, Sayings and Oral Narratives”, explored the diversity of tribal oral traditions, including songs, myths, riddles and tales. The session was moderated by Prof. Sylvanus Lamare, with Dr. Lisa Lomdak, Mr. Anuja Mohan Pradhan and Ms. Swati Anand as discussants.
Drawing on her research in Arunachal Pradesh,
Dr. Lisa Lomdak
spoke of the custodians of oral traditions, such as the Nyibu, Midi and Abatani, and Njik-Njegam, who preserve knowledge through memory rather than writing. She highlighted the role of women as repositories of oral tradition, preserving narratives through songs during daily chores, marriages and funerals. She underlined that researchers must publish sacred traditions and knowledge only with explicit community permission.
Mr. Anuja Mohan Pradhan
, representing the Kui-speaking community of Odisha, said that the Kui language has a rich oral heritage of creation myths, riddles and songs, but is gradually disappearing due to the lack of a formal script and the pressures of modern multilingualism. He shared a traditional Kui riddle and folk tales, including one that symbolises how tribal communities risk losing their roots and culture to outside influences.
Ms. Swati Anand
shared the cultural heritage of Bastar, Chhattisgarh, including the Bastar Madai festival and local legends of protective deities, which continue to live in community memory and practice.
In his concluding remarks, the moderator made three suggestions: linking all state tribal affairs websites to the Ministry’s main portal; digitising and making accessible information on tribal communities available with the international institutions and libraries; and scientifically studying and documenting tribal scientific and engineering knowledge, such as the living root bridges of Meghalaya.
On Day 2, the festival will hold sessions on oral epics and heroic traditions and on oral tradition in multilingual education, along with story and poetry readings in various tribal languages, followed by the valedictory session.

title: Ministry of Tribal Affairs launches national initiative for conservation of medicinal plants and promotion of sustainable livelihoods in 16 tribal hotspots across 13 States/UTs
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 NOV 2026 6:36PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Government of India, in collaboration with the CSIR–National Botanical Research Institute (CSIR-NBRI), Lucknow, formally launched the project “Integrated Conservation, Agro-Technology and Bioresource Enterprise Development for Sustainable Tribal Livelihoods in Tribal Hotspots of India” at the Central University of Odisha, Koraput, on 12 November 2026.
The inaugural programme was attended by Additional Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, senior officials of the Ministry, Dr. Ajit Kumar Kumar Shasany, Hon’ble Vice-Chancellor of the Central University of Odisha, Dr. Sharad Kumar Srivastava, Chief Scientist and Principal Investigator, CSIR-National Botanical Research Institute, Lucknow,
Ms. Snehaprabha Majhi, ITDA Project Administration, Koraput
, scientists from ICMR-National Institute of Health Research, Bhubaneshwar, scientists, experts, industry representatives, faculty members, and tribal community representatives.
The three-year initiative aims to conserve the rich medicinal plant biodiversity of tribal regions while harnessing traditional knowledge and indigenous bioresources to create sustainable livelihood and enterprise opportunities for tribal communities. The project covers 16 selected tribal hotspots across 13 States/Union Territories: Alluri Seetharama Raju (Andhra Pradesh), Kokrajhar (Assam), Narayanpur (Chhattisgarh), Navsari (Gujarat), East Singhbhum (Jharkhand), Kodagu (Karnataka), Wayanad (Kerala), Kargil (Ladakh), Anuppur (Madhya Pradesh), Gadchiroli and Nashik (Maharashtra), Kandhamal, Balangir and Koraput (Odisha), Sonbhadra (Uttar Pradesh), and Dharchula (Uttarakhand).
The major interventions under the project include documentation of approximately 200–300 medicinal plant species, scientific propagation of 30–40 rare, endangered and threatened (RET) species, establishment of 16 community nurseries and 16 seed banks, and development of community-level capacities for medicinal plant cultivation and bioresource-based enterprises. The project also envisages distribution of 40,000–50,000 quality planting materials to support conservation, propagation and sustainable cultivation.
As part of the initial implementation, CSIR-NBRI has already undertaken fieldwork in Sonbhadra district of Uttar Pradesh during October 2026. The field team interacted with 146 tribal knowledge holders across 12 villages and documented traditional medicinal practices. A total of 97 field numbers, representing approximately 200 medicinal and economically important plant samples, were collected. Additionally, 25 live orchid samples were collected for germplasm conservation and multiplication at the CSIR-NBRI Botanical Garden.
The initiative seeks to establish strong linkages between scientific institutions, Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs), State Tribal Welfare and Forest Departments and local communities. Special emphasis will be placed on involving tribal farmers, traditional healers, women and rural youth in conservation, capacity building, cultivation and value-chain development.
A special technical session titled “From Tribal Knowledge to Enterprise” was organised as part of the programme, bringing together experts and stakeholders to deliberate on translating traditional knowledge and medicinal plant resources into sustainable economic opportunities. The programme also includes interaction with tribal farmers and traditional knowledge holders, followed by a field visit to the Koraput tribal hotspot on 13 November 2026.
Through this initiative, the Ministry aims to create a replicable institutional model that integrates biodiversity conservation, scientific research, preservation of indigenous knowledge and community-led enterprise development. The project represents an important step towards recognising tribal communities as custodians of India’s biological and traditional knowledge heritage while enabling them to derive sustainable economic benefits from their local bioresources.

title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA INTERACTS WITH MERITORIOUS EMRS STUDENTS AT RASHTRAPATI BHAVAN
subtitle: President Droupadi Murmu urges students to pursue excellence, remain connected with their roots and contribute to the development of their communities
date:

content:
The Hon’ble President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, interacted with meritorious students and alumni of Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) at the Rashtrapati Bhavan Cultural Centre (RBCC), Rashtrapati Bhavan, New Delhi, on 12 November 2026. The programme was organised by the National Education Society for Tribal Students (NESTS), Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Government of India, as part of Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada 2026, commemorating the 151st birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda.
The interaction provided an opportunity for students from different parts of the country to share their academic achievements, educational journeys, experiences and aspirations with the Hon’ble President. The programme also highlighted the role of EMRS in providing quality education and enabling tribal students to pursue higher education and professional careers.
Referring to the significance of Eklavya, the Hon’ble President encouraged students to understand the values associated with his life and draw inspiration from them. She observed that EMRS are providing tribal students with opportunities to develop their abilities and talents. She also noted that the equal representation of boys and girls in EMRS reflects progress towards inclusive development.
The Hon’ble President particularly emphasised the importance of remaining connected with one's roots, identity and cultural heritage. She encouraged them to take pride in their tribal heritage and maintain a strong connection with their villages and communities.
The Hon’ble President further advised students that, after acquiring higher education and establishing themselves as doctors, engineers, administrators and professionals in different fields, they should contribute to the welfare and development of their villages and communities. She stressed that their education would have greater significance when its benefits reach the people and regions from where they come.
Shri Jual Oram, Union Minister of Tribal Affairs, delivered the welcome address. Addressing the gathering,  Union Minister encouraged students to aim high and pursue their aspirations with dedication, discipline, hard work and self-confidence.
A total of 146 meritorious students and alumni from EMRS across the country participated in the programme. The participants included Class X and XII toppers and students who had secured admission to premier institutions such as IITs, NITs, National Law Universities (NLUs), NIFT and government medical colleges.
On the occasion, NESTS showcased a five-minute short film featuring the success stories of EMRS students and their journeys from their schools to the realisation of their dreams. Students also shared their educational journeys and experiences with the gathering, highlighting the role of EMRS in providing a supportive learning environment, academic opportunities, exposure and facilities that have contributed to their personal and academic development.
The programme also recognised the contributions of officials and institutions associated with the implementation of the EMRS initiative. The Hon’ble President felicitated the Secretaries/Principal Secretaries of the Tribal Welfare Departments of Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Odisha; five District Magistrates; and Principals of five best-performing EMRS. Awards were also conferred upon best-performing tribal startups in recognition of their contributions to entrepreneurship and innovation.
The interaction highlighted the importance of providing quality education, equal opportunities and appropriate institutional support to tribal students. It also reinforced the role of EMRS in nurturing academic excellence, confidence, leadership and professional aspirations among tribal youth, while encouraging them to preserve their cultural identity and contribute to the development of their communities.

date:

                12 NOV 2026 7:45PM by PIB Delhi
content:
NITI Aayog today released the report titled “Impact Assessment of PLI Schemes”, prepared in collaboration with the Indian Institute of Management, Ahmedabad as the knowledge partner. The report recognizes the PLI Scheme as a flagship policy intervention launched by the Government of India to enhance India’s manufacturing competitiveness, integrate Indian firms into global value chains, and accelerate the journey towards an Atmanirbhar Bharat. By providing production-linked incentives to a select set of high-performing firms, the scheme is designed to be self-sustaining, encouraging adoption of advanced technologies, capacity creation, and sustained growth in output and exports.
Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes, implemented by various Ministries and Departments, have emerged as a successful initiative for scaling up domestic manufacturing, investment and production, while strengthening India’s position in global value chains by driving exports, building domestic capabilities and enhancing competitiveness. Acting as a catalyst for industrial deepening, employment and export expansion, the initiative is advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 through a globally competitive manufacturing sector.
The report presents a sector-wise assessment of the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme across all 14 sectors notified by the Government of India, examining its impact on the key parameters of investment, additional production, exports, and employment generation. The assessment is based on sector-wise collection of firm-level data shared by implementing Ministries, supplemented by industry-level inputs from authenticated sources. Sectoral outcomes have been categorized into four broad groups: On-Track, Partial Impact, Insignificant Evidence of Impact, and Data unavailable; providing a structured and comparative overview of the scheme’s progress across sectors.
The report finds that sectors with strong industry participation have demonstrated encouraging outcomes under the scheme. Pharmaceuticals, Mobile Manufacturing under Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing (LSEM), Food Processing, Telecom, White Goods, Automobiles and Drones have shown notable progress in investment, production and capacity creation, with the Drones sector emerging as an early implementation success.
Manufacturing capacity in High Efficiency Solar PV Modules has also expanded significantly, reflecting growing domestic capability and strengthening India’s renewable energy manufacturing ecosystem. The report further notes that sectors involving advanced and emerging technologies such as ACC Batteries, Specialty Steel and Technical Textiles are witnessing gradual capacity creation and ecosystem development, which are expected to contribute significantly to India’s long-term industrial growth trajectory. Across sectors, the scheme has played an important role in stimulating investment, enhancing manufacturing capacity and strengthening industrial competitiveness.
The report also highlights the importance of continued focus on deeper MSME participation, harmonized data systems and sustained ecosystem development to further strengthen sectoral outcomes and support long-term manufacturing growth.
Overall sectoral analysis suggests that nearly 70% of targeted segments are on track. The scheme has successfully stimulated investment and production beyond targets, though its long-term effectiveness will depend on deepening domestic value addition and strengthening supply chains.
By providing a structured, evidence-based and sector-specific assessment of the PLI Scheme, the report is expected to serve as a useful reference for policymakers, implementing Ministries, industry stakeholders and researchers in shaping a globally competitive, employment-generating and self-reliant manufacturing sector for India under the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.

Food Security Without Boundaries
From Portability to Inclusion: Transforming Foodgrain Access
The
One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC)
scheme was launched in 2019 by the Department of Food & Public Distribution. It is a major reform of the
Public Distribution System (PDS)
, enabling nationwide portability of ration cards
and beneficiaries covered under the National Food Security Act (NFSA).
NFSA establishes legal entitlements for subsidized food grains, while
TPDS
distributes these grains to eligible
beneficiaries.
Under
Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS)
reforms, ONORC uses technology to enable beneficiaries to access their entitled foodgrains anywhere in the country.
The initiative has strengthened social protection for migrant populations and advanced the vision of a more integrated, inclusive, and beneficiary-centric welfare delivery system.
Enables access to foodgrain entitlements from any Fair Price Shop across the country without needing a new ration card. Makes foodgrain entitlements portable across States.
Supports migrant workers and families in accessing PDS benefits after changing residence.
Ensures subsidized foodgrain access for beneficiaries wherever they reside.
Strengthens PDS access for NFSA beneficiaries across the country.
Portability Milestones
ONORC has transformed PDS by making foodgrain access seamless, portable, and nationwide.
ONORC has been implemented across all 36 States/UTs, covering 100% of PMGKAY beneficiaries.
ONORC facilitates approximately
3.27 crore portability transactions every month
.
Since its inception, it has recorded over
233 crore inter-state and intra-state portability transactions
, distributing more than
614 LMT of foodgrains
.
Strengthening Transparency and Delivery Under PDS
The Government has complemented ration portability with digital authentication, data-driven targeting and technology-enabled distribution to improve transparency and last-mile delivery.
100% Digitisation:
Ration card and beneficiary databases are
100% digitised
across all States/UTs as
of October 2026
, covering around
78.65 crore
beneficiaries, and are accessible on public transparency portals of States/UTs. Out of
20.51 crore ration cards
in the Central System,
98.8% (20.27 crore)
have been
Aadhaar-seeded
. The total number of beneficiaries seeded with Aadhaar stands at
76.97 crore.
As on 30 September 2026, e-KYC has been done in respect of
71.52 crore
beneficiaries i.e.,
91% of total beneficiaries.
Transparent Grievance Redressal:
Transparency portals, online grievance systems and toll-free helplines operate across all States/UTs.
Computerised Supply Chain:
Online foodgrain allocation is implemented nationwide, while supply chains are computerised in
31 States/UTs
.
ePoS-enabled FPSs
: Out of a total of
5.51 lakh Fair Price Shops (FPSs)
,
99.8% (5.50 lakh)
are operational with
e-PoS devices
.

Mera Ration App: Foodgrain Access at Your Fingertips
As part of technology-driven TPDS reforms under ONORC, the Department launched the
Mera Ration
mobile application. Available in
13 languages
, the app helps beneficiaries access important ration-related information and services.
Key features include:
Check monthly foodgrain entitlement details
View past transaction details
Verify Aadhaar-seeding status
Check eligibility for national portability
Register voluntarily for ONORC
Locate nearby Fair Price Shops (FPSs) using GPS
Navigate to the nearest FPS through the map
Mera Ration app helps beneficiaries, particularly migrants, locate nearby FPSs and access their foodgrain entitlements in a new area.
Toward Inclusive and Dignified Food Security
ONORC has transformed the Public Distribution System by making foodgrain access portable, nationwide and technology-enabled. Its implementation across all 36 States/UTs, along with extensive portability transactions, reflects its growing role in strengthening food security.  With digitalised beneficiary databases, ePoS-enabled Fair Price Shops, SARTHAK-PDS framework, and the Mera Ration app, the system is becoming more transparent, integrated, and beneficiary-centric.
Collectively, these reforms are strengthening last-mile delivery and ensuring that food security reaches beneficiaries wherever they live and work.
